title: Tool Calling & Planner/Executor
summary: Agents act by calling tools. Planner/executor patterns separate deciding what to do from doing it — with schemas, permissions, and retries that look a lot like distributed systems design.

sections.title: Tools as APIs
paragraphs: Each tool needs a schema, authz, timeout, and idempotency story. The LLM proposes calls; your runtime validates and executes.

sections.title: Planner vs executor
paragraphs: Planners produce steps; executors run tools and return observations. Loops continue until stop conditions. Bound steps and tokens.

sections.title: Safety
paragraphs: Least privilege tools. Human approval for irreversible actions. Sandbox code execution. Log every call for audit.

sections.title: Reliability
paragraphs: Tool failures need retries with budgets. Partial success in multi-tool plans needs compensating actions — sagas again.

deepDive.title: Tool Calling & Planner/Executor — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Tool Calling & Planner/Executor in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Tool Calling & Planner/Executor — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Tool Calling & Planner/Executor include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Tool Calling & Planner/Executor — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Tool Calling & Planner/Executor intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

whyItMatters: Agent products are distributed systems that can take irreversible actions — design them accordingly.
reflectionQuestions: Which tools require human approval in your agent?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
